title: Direct power compact transport agrees with repeated transport
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, integers $a,n\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its fixed algebraic closure $k$, and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the chosen algebraic closure, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and write $a_X:X\to s$. Use $D^b_c(X,A)$ and the compact-support functor $H(M)=R\Gamma_c(X,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}M)$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$, $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ as in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and $P_r=L(g^r)^*$, $T=P_1$, with derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Fix one compactification $c_0=(X_0\hookrightarrow\overline X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0)$ of $a_{X_0}$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and use its base change $c$ to represent $Ra_{X!}$ for every power.

For every $r\geq1$ let $\tau^{(r)}_{c,M}:H(M)\to H(P_rM)$ be the specified direct compact-support transport of [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition]: the point transport along $h^r$ followed by the point fiber of the compactification exchange for the $r$-th-power square, using this same $c_0$. Write $\tau_{c,M}=\tau^{(1)}_{c,M}$ for the degree-one transport of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport].

Use the actual canonical comparisons $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}T^r$ of [def-trf-frobenius-pullback-power-comparison], normalized by $T^1=T$, $T^{r+1}=T\circ T^r$, and $d_1=\mathrm{id}_T$. For $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and $r\geq1$ set
$$S_{r,M}=H(d_{r,M}^{-1})\circ\tau_{c,T^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{c,M},$$
where the repeated transport has exactly $r$ factors (and $T^0=\mathrm{id}$). Then every $P_rM$ and $T^rM$ lies in $D^b_c(X,A)$, and the following equality holds in the derived category of finite $A$-module coefficient complexes:
$$S_{r,M}=\tau^{(r)}_{c,M}.$$
Both sides are isomorphisms $H(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(P_rM)$. No Weil structure or finite Tor-amplitude condition on $M$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply clause 1 of [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] to the structure morphism of X_0: g is an isomorphism with the specified inverse. Each g^r is therefore an isomorphism, with inverse (g^{-1})^r. Since ell is invertible in k, the finite-coefficient clause of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] gives P_r M in D^b_c(X,A). Applying its degree-one case repeatedly gives T^r M in that category, starting with T^0 M=M. Thus P_r and T restrict to endofunctors of this full subcategory, and the actual natural comparisons restrict as well.

proof.text: Retain the given c_0 throughout. Set eta_M=tau_{c,M}; [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] states its naturality. With b_r=c_r, the inverse of the canonical comparison P_{r+1} to T P_r, [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition] gives tau^{(1)}=eta and tau^{(r+1)}_M=H(b_{r,M}) eta_{P_r M} tau^{(r)}_M. These are the specified direct exchanges, rather than maps defined by this recurrence. For the actual d_r of [def-trf-frobenius-pullback-power-comparison]: in its recursion d_{r+1}=T(d_r)∘C_{1,r} the composite is defined only when C_{1,r} has codomain T∘P_r, so C_{1,r} is the canonical comparison c_{g,g^r}:P_{r+1}→T∘P_r (the displayed P_b∘P_a of that node is read this way). Hence the recursion splits g^{r+1} into r+1 copies of g by canonical composition comparisons with d_1=id, and the independence clause of [lem-trf-frobenius-pullback-comparison-coherence] identifies it with the d_r of that lemma, which gives d_{r+1}^{-1} T(d_r)=b_r. Both cited statements use the same canonical pullback-composition comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-frobenius-transport-induction] with C=D^b_c(X,A), D the derived category of finite A-module coefficient complexes, H=R Gamma_c(X,-) of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], T=P_1, eta=tau_c and tau_r=tau^{(r)}_c. Step 1 verifies the functor domains, and step 2 supplies every recurrence and normalization hypothesis. The lemma identifies exactly H(d_{r,M}^{-1}) eta_{T^{r-1}M} ... eta_M with tau^{(r)}_{c,M} for all positive r. This is the asserted equality S_{r,M}=tau^{(r)}_{c,M}, in the derived category before taking cohomology.

source.place: Proof, second sentence, compact-support transport along g_gamma^m; explicit assembly of the returned proof paragraphs 2-3

proof.text: For each j from 0 to r-1, clause 3 of [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso], at Lambda=A and the object T^j M from step 1, makes eta_{T^j M} invertible. Since d_{r,M} is an isomorphism, H(d_{r,M}^{-1}) has inverse H(d_{r,M}). The inverse of their composite S_{r,M} is the reversed composite of these inverses. Step 3 therefore makes tau^{(r)}_{c,M} an isomorphism too. None of the cited finite-level assertions requires a Weil structure or finite Tor-amplitude.
